doc.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Opening and Mance's current recording with Enja
summary: Welcome and introductions; Mance describes his own trio and his Enja and Chiaroscuro records.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We are here today filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive, with Dr. Michael Woods from our faculty, and we have the pleasure of the company of Mr. Junior Mance, who is a veteran pianist, teacher, composer, expert on the blues, and it’s a great pleasure to have you here. Welcome.
Thank you. It’s a pleasure to be here.
I’d like to start off asking you what you’re up to now.

Well now I’m up to several things. I’m still performing with my own trio and I’m recording for Enja Records. It’s spelled E-N-J-A, over here they say “Inja,” but in Europe they say “Enia.” And also I’ve been, before that I decided, in fact I had two records come out at the same time, one on Enja and one on Chiaroscuro.
Which we have with us today for your autograph.
